title: Define graceful degradation modes for Hosted overload protection (fallback + feature reduction)
creator: Nikhil Sharma
project: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (Reliability Program)
description:
Background
Hosted API overload protection will sometimes need to preserve platform SLOs by rejecting traffic (429/503) and, when configured, degrading safely instead of timing out. This ticket defines the *allowed* degradation modes (fallback routing + feature reduction) and the controls/guardrails required so that:
- Customers do not experience silent or confusing behavior changes.
- Tenants remain isolated (no noisy-neighbor incentive loops).
- Degradation does not create retry storms or multi-hop cascades.
- We have clear eligibility rules, observability, and support playbooks.

Scope
This is a product definition / policy ticket. Engineering implementation is tracked in ENG tickets and ADRs.

Definitions
- “Degradation” = serving a response that differs from the original request intent/config in order to maintain availability and latency SLOs.
- “Fallback” = routing a request to a compatible model variant and/or alternate region per pre-configured policy.
- “Feature reduction” = applying pre-configured caps/disablements to non-essential or high-cost features under duress.
- “Duress” signals = breaker open, shed policy active, runtime saturation, or dependency brownout (as defined by the policy engine).

Goals
- Provide a small, explicit set of degradation modes with stable semantics.
- Require opt-in (tier default + tenant override) and strong transparency when degradation is applied.
- Ensure engineering has crisp constraints (what’s allowed, what’s prohibited, what must be surfaced in responses/logs).

Non-goals
- No new billing behavior (we may reduce output, but do not alter billing rules here).
- No new customer-facing API surface beyond additive headers/fields in error or success payloads.

Allowed degradation modes (v1)
A) Fallback routing (preferred when configured)
1) Model fallback (same region)
- Description: Route to a compatible model variant when the primary model is overloaded/unavailable.
- Examples:
  - “rw/llama-3.1-70b-instruct@pinned” -> “rw/llama-3.1-70b-instruct@stable” (different serving profile)
  - “rw/qwen2.5-72b-instruct” -> “rw/qwen2.5-32b-instruct” (capacity-available smaller variant)
- Requirements:
  - Must be explicitly configured via policy (no implicit fallback).
  - Must be compatibility-checked (chat vs completions, tool-calling capability, context window, JSON mode/structured output support).
  - Must preserve safety settings (e.g., system prompt handling, moderation policy) to the same or stricter behavior.

2) Region fallback (same model)
- Description: Route to another region with available capacity.
- Requirements:
  - Only if tenant policy allows cross-region processing.
  - Data residency constraints must be enforced (deny rather than degrade if not permitted).
  - Must include loop-prevention and bounded attempts (see Guardrails).

3) Combined fallback (model + region)
- Description: If allowed by policy, attempt model fallback in-region first; if still overloaded and cross-region is allowed, attempt regional fallback.
- Requirements:
  - Deterministic ordering defined in policy.
  - Bounded retries; no “ping-pong” across regions.

B) Feature reduction (only behind policy flags; must be transparent)
Feature reduction is applied when:
- Fallback is not configured OR fallback is exhausted/blocked by constraints.
- Request would otherwise be shed with overload error.

Allowed feature reduction knobs (v1)
1) max_tokens cap
- Reduce max_tokens to a configured cap under duress.
- Applies to: chat/completions.
- Guardrail: cap must be >= a minimum floor to avoid breaking typical short responses (floor TBD per tier; initial proposal: 128 for self-serve, 256 for enterprise Hosted unless overridden).

2) Disable/limit tool calling complexity
- Options:
  - Disallow tool calls entirely (return overload error with actionable guidance) OR
  - Limit number of tool calls / tool schema size.
- Important: We should *not* silently ignore tools. If tools are required by the request, and we cannot honor them, return an explicit overload error code rather than partial behavior.

3) Streaming concurrency reduction (server-side)
- Reduce per-tenant concurrent streaming sessions (or per-route) under duress.
- Behavior: new streaming requests may be shed with 429/503 per policy; we do not downgrade streaming->non-streaming automatically in v1.

4) Disable optional diagnostics features
- Examples: logprobs, verbose usage breakdown fields (if they add material cost), extended tracing.
- Guardrail: must be purely additive/optional fields; disabling cannot break clients that follow docs.

Not allowed in v1 (explicitly prohibited)
- Silent switch from streaming to non-streaming.
- Silent disabling of tools when tools are requested.
- Changing customer-requested temperature/top_p/system prompts.
- Truncating input prompts (other than rejecting with explicit input-length error).
- Switching an endpoint type (chat <-> completions) or returning a different output schema.
- Cross-tenant pooling or any behavior that violates tenant isolation.

Controls & configuration requirements
1) Opt-in model
- Degradation must be controllable at three levels:
  - Tier default (self-serve Hosted vs enterprise Hosted vs Dedicated)
  - Tenant override (allow/deny specific degradation modes)
  - Route/model selector (e.g., allow fallback for embeddings but not chat; allow model fallback but not region fallback)

2) Policy engine representation
- Each degradation mode must map to an explicit policy flag with a clear name and auditability.
- All policies must have safe defaults (prefer rejection with clear overload error over silent degradation).

3) Response transparency
When degradation occurs (fallback or feature reduction), we must surface it in a consistent way:
- Response header: `x-redwood-degraded: true`
- Response header: `x-redwood-degradation-mode: fallback_model | fallback_region | cap_max_tokens | tool_calling_limited | ...`
- Response header: `x-redwood-request-id` (already standard) and correlation ID must be present.
- Optional additive field in JSON response (if product/eng agree): `degradation: "..."`.

4) Customer controls surfaced (enterprise)
- For enterprise Hosted/Dedicated customers, degradation settings must be configurable via Console (or via support-managed config) with an explicit description of tradeoffs.

Guardrails (must-haves)
1) Bounded attempts and loop prevention
- Routing must cap fallback attempts (proposal: max 1 model fallback + max 1 region fallback; no more than 2 attempts).
- Must record “attempt chain” in logs/trace to support debugging.

2) Avoid retry storms
- If we shed after attempting allowed degradation, the final response must include Retry-After when applicable and use stable overload error codes.
- Do not encourage immediate retries when saturation is systemic.

3) Data residency / compliance constraints
- Region fallback is blocked unless tenant policy explicitly allows it.
- If blocked, do not attempt region fallback; proceed to feature reduction or return overload error.

4) Quality / correctness constraints
- Fallback models must meet a minimum compatibility bar for the requested features (structured output, tool calling, context window).
- If compatibility check fails, do not fallback; prefer explicit error code indicating “fallback unavailable for requested features”.

5) Tenant isolation
- Degradation modes must not create a situation where a single tenant can disproportionately consume shared capacity (e.g., unlimited fallback attempts or excessive queueing).

6) Observability & supportability
- Every degraded response must increment a metric tagged by mode/tier/route (bounded cardinality).
- Support must have a dashboard view to confirm: whether a tenant is degraded, which mode is active, and which regions/models were involved.

Open questions (need alignment)
- Do we want to allow “queued admission” as a degradation mode (e.g., short server-side queue with a timeout) in v1, or keep it out-of-scope until after GA?
- Should max_tokens cap return an explicit warning to clients in the payload, or header-only is sufficient?
- Minimum floors per tier for max_tokens cap.
- Whether to allow streaming->non-streaming downgrade in v2 (likely no, but revisit).

Proposed rollout and comms
- Dark launch: metrics only; do not apply degradation unless explicitly enabled for internal tenants.
- Canary: enable fallback for a small set of tenants with known spiky traffic; keep feature reduction disabled unless needed.
- GA: publish docs for headers/fields and recommended client behavior.

Links
- ADR-014: Hosted overload error taxonomy (status mapping, Retry-After semantics)
- ENG-4824: Routing fallback on overload
- ENG-4822: Define overload error codes and payloads

acceptance_criteria: List of allowed degradation modes (fallback + feature reduction) is documented with clear definitions and requirements.
Explicit list of prohibited behaviors (no silent tool disablement, no streaming downgrade, etc.) is agreed by PM/Eng/SRE.
Controls are defined at tier/tenant/route-model levels, with opt-in defaults and policy engine mapping guidance.
Transparency requirements are defined (headers/optional fields) for when degradation is applied.
Guardrails for loop prevention, bounded attempts, data residency constraints, and observability are documented.
Open questions are enumerated with owners and target decision dates.
comments: 2025-11-04 (Nikhil Sharma): Added explicit prohibition on silent tool-disable; if tools requested and cannot be honored under duress, we should return a clear overload error with Retry-After rather than partial behavior.

2025-11-07 (Mina Haddad): Routing can support at most 2 attempts without adding significant tail latency. Strongly prefer deterministic policy order: in-region model fallback first, then region fallback if permitted. Need compatibility matrix from product for structured output + tool calling.
2025-11-09 (Rafael Mendes): Please require `x-redwood-degraded` and mode header for *all* degraded successes. SRE wants a single counter metric keyed by mode/tier/route (no tenant label).

2025-11-12 (Wei Chen): Docs can cover new headers and client guidance, but we should keep payload changes additive and minimal. Header-only is fine for v1; include examples for both fallback and token cap.

2025-11-14 (Lauren Bishop): For enterprise Hosted, region fallback must be an explicit customer contract item due to residency. Suggest Console UI defaults to OFF with a short explanation and link to data residency docs.
